grh_d767426dd9bfb7a53f98.title: A Game of Cat and Mouse
paragraphs: Nineteen-year-old Bo Henshaw escapes from a psychiatric hospital and goes on the run, while his father Matt and brother Davey race the police to find him first. Matt distrusts the institution and insists that the family should handle Bo themselves, even after learning that Bo has killed a woman and stolen a car. Knowing Bo's obsession with automobiles, they trace him toward a county fair and speedway, where he imagines he can become a race driver. Bo obtains a gun and threatens officers when they corner him, forcing an officer to shoot him. Matt then seizes the gun and holds the police at bay rather than allow medical help. Bo dies from his wound, and Matt calls for revenge, but Davey finally refuses to continue the cycle, returns the officers' weapons and accepts that more violence or running away will change nothing.

[[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Barney Phillips, William Zuckert, Byron Kane, John Shay, and Lou Horne. Other credited names include Elliott Lewis as director, Elliott Lewis as producer, Ralph Goodman as writer, and [[person|vincent-price|Vincent Price]] as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_d7cbf130b8e6ee9914f9.title: The Advancement of Vern Berwick
paragraphs: Vern Berwick is a thirty-two-year-old auto-parts clerk whose extraordinary memory has always seemed more odd than useful. After taking a speed-reading course, he begins absorbing entire libraries and his instructor realizes that his ability is far beyond ordinary intelligence. Vern's rapidly developing mind attracts government attention, and he is eventually selected for an interstellar mission to Andromeda. He accepts even after learning that relativity means only a few years will pass for him while decades pass on Earth, so everyone he knows will be gone when he returns. On launch, however, the ship's computer surprises him by reproducing the familiar nagging voices of his parents, giving the newly advanced Vern an absurd reminder of the home he thought he was escaping.

grh_d7b5811492e651660877.title: Requiem For A Hero
paragraphs: Father John Mulligan visits a condemned murderer who uses the same name and is wearing a unique family ring. The priest realizes the prisoner may be the infant son he believed lost at sea decades earlier, before he entered the priesthood. Dr. Christian questions the man, who claims the ring belonged to another rescued child named Eddie Graham and convinces Father John that Eddie, later a decorated serviceman killed in the South Pacific, was his true son. After the priest leaves comforted, Dr. Christian exposes the prisoner's deception: the man himself was the baby from the lifeboat and used an old photograph from the parcel to describe Father John's wife. Facing death, he chose to give his father a heroic son to remember rather than the shame of knowing a murderer was his child. Dr. Christian keeps the secret and tells him that his sacrifice was itself an act of heroism.
This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on February 6, 1946. It is listed as episode 376 in the archive.
The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes.
